items.name: ready
items.text: Wait for the core to open. Properties such as core.length are populated afterwards. You rarely need it, because every method waits for it itself.

items.name: close
items.text: Close the core and release its resources. Close every session you open.

items.name: append
items.text: Append one block, or an array of blocks as a batch. Returns the new length and byte length.

items.name: createWriteStream
items.text: A writable stream where each chunk becomes a block.

items.name: truncate
items.text: Shorten the core. By default this raises the fork id by one.

items.name: clear
items.text: Clear stored blocks from your local copy to reclaim space. Peers you are connected to are told you no longer have them.

items.name: get
items.text: Get a block. If it is not local, wait for it to download. Options include wait, timeout and valueEncoding.

items.name: has
items.text: True if the core holds every block from start up to end.

items.name: count
items.text: How many blocks in that range are stored locally.

items.name: seek
items.text: Find the block that contains a byte offset.

items.name: createReadStream
items.text: A readable stream of blocks.

items.name: createByteStream
items.text: A readable stream over a range of bytes, with byteOffset and byteLength options.

items.name: update
items.text: Wait for the core to learn of a new length from peers.

items.name: info
items.text: Information about the core, such as its size in bytes.

items.name: replicate
items.text: Make a replication stream. Pipe it to another core's stream, one side as initiator and the other not.

items.name: download
items.text: Ask for a range of blocks, or a list with { blocks: [4, 9, 7] }. Await range.done() for a finite range.

items.name: findingPeers
items.text: Tell the core you are looking for peers. Call done() when a discovery round ends.

items.name: session
items.text: A new instance sharing the same underlying core. Close it when done.

items.name: snapshot
items.text: Like a session, but backed by a storage snapshot: it will not append or truncate.

items.name: treeHash
items.text: The Merkle tree hash of the core at a length, by default its current length.

items.name: key
items.text: Buffer holding the public key that identifies the core.

items.name: discoveryKey
items.text: A key derived from the public key. It finds peers without leaking the key that verifies the data.

items.name: length
items.text: How many blocks the core holds.

items.name: fork
items.text: The current fork id. It increases when the core is truncated.

items.name: writable
items.text: True if you can append to or truncate this core.

items.name: readable
items.text: True if you can read from this core. False after closing.

items.name: contiguousLength
items.text: How many blocks are available without a gap from the start.

items.name: peers
items.text: The peers currently connected to this core.

items.name: MAX_SUGGESTED_BLOCK_SIZE
items.text: The suggested maximum block size, 15 MB (15,728,640 bytes), so blocks replicate smoothly.

items.name: append
items.text: The core got a new length, locally or from a peer.

items.name: truncate
items.text: The core was truncated, locally or by a peer.

items.name: download
items.text: A block arrived from a peer.

items.name: upload
items.text: A block was sent to a peer.

items.name: peer-add
items.text: A new peer connected.

items.name: peer-remove
items.text: A peer disconnected.
